facts.statement: The genus Agkistracanthus was described by Duffin and Furrer in 1981.
The genus Agkistracanthus contains only one known species, A. mitgelensis.
facts.quote: It currently contains a single species, A. mitgelensis

facts.statement: Agkistracanthus lived during the Rhaetian to Hettangian epochs, covering the transition from the Triassic to the Jurassic period.
facts.quote: It is known from the Rhaetian to Hettangian epochs, spanning the transition from the Triassic to Jurassic period

facts.statement: Fossils of Agkistracanthus have been found in Switzerland, Austria, and Britain.
facts.quote: Fossils from this genus are known from Switzerland, Austria, and Britain

facts.statement: Knowledge of Agkistracanthus comes mostly from isolated and fragmentary fossils, including fin spines and parts of the skull and jaws.
facts.quote: It is known mostly from isolated and fragmentary material, including fin spines as well as palatine, symphyseal, and mandibular structures

facts.statement: Agkistracanthus belongs to the family Myriacanthidae.
Agkistracanthus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Agkistracanthus lived between 205.7 and 199.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Hettangian (205.7 to 199.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Agkistracanthus is an extinct genus of holocephalan cartilaginous fish.
rejected.quote: Agkistracanthus is an extinct genus of holocephalan cartilaginous fish
